text:
ConocoPhillips fell 1.1% today to $135.72, giving back gains from the prior two sessions despite oil prices holding steady around $91–96 per barrel. The stock had rallied sharply on September 1st and 2nd as tensions between Iran and Kuwait escalated—driving U.S. crude up more than 9% for the week—but today's pullback suggests that initial geopolitical premium is cooling slightly now that the immediate headline risk has passed without dramatic expansion of the conflict.

The broader backdrop remains supportive for the oil sector: crude is still up meaningfully week-over-week, and Middle East supply risks haven't fully resolved. However, the momentum stalled today, likely because markets are digesting Trump's comment that renewed hostilities won't last "too long," which may have eased near-term supply disruption fears that had driven the earlier rally.
